verdict.rationale: Stripe Identity documents an API to create verification sessions, track their status with webhook events, and retrieve extracted data and images programmatically with a secret key, so an agent can drive the core pipeline over the API. A general Stripe MCP server exists, but nothing shows it exposes Identity tools, and the evidence never mentions scoped or restricted credentials or an API-triggered re-check (status override is described as a manual review tool). missing for 10: documented re-check or re-verify API action, scoped/restricted key support for Identity, evidence that the MCP server covers Identity sessions, independent hands-on agent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate the verification pipeline — create sessions, poll outcomes, retrieve extracted data, and trigger re-checks through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: This API tracks a verification, from initial creation through the entire verification process, and shows verification results upon completion.
Stripe generates events every time a session changes status.
You can access most verification details programmatically... using your secret key.
The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API
